Hi Julian —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, and then a suggested language block you can paste into your procurement ticket.

1) Platform fee scope: for hybrid deployments the platform fee is applied to the committed VPC (reserved) capacity only. Bursts to Redwood-hosted capacity are billed separately as metered tokens/compute at the metered rate unless you choose to pre-purchase credits that apply to those bursts.

2) Splitting committed spend: yes — we commonly structure a committed contract as (a) a fixed platform fee that covers the private control plane, support, and baseline engineering entitlements, plus (b) a pool of metered infra credits that apply to burst usage or overage. Conversion guidance (starter bundle): $1 of committed spend typically converts to ~$0.85 worth of metered-usage value after admin/ops allocation. We can make that more aggressive for larger commits.

3) Credit rollover: unused credits from the committed pool can be used toward ephemeral hosted bursts within the contract year, but they do not roll beyond the 12-month term unless expressly agreed.

Procurement note (paste):
Redwood Inference will provide Medisync a 12-month Private deployment agreement that consists of: (1) a committed monthly platform fee covering reserved VPC capacity and support entitlements; and (2) a matched pool of metered infra credits to cover occasional burst execution on Redwood-hosted capacity. Metered credits apply to hosted burst usage during the term and do not auto-roll beyond the contract period. Detailed terms and SOW are attached.

I'll loop in pricing to propose concrete numbers for your starter bundle.

Best,
Naomi

Redwood Inference

- For a 12-mo starter commit around $200k ARR, we typically propose a platform fee that represents ~35-40% of the committed ARR, with the remainder allocated to metered credits. That leaves room for the customer to consume bursts without hitting a high overage rate.
- If they want credits to act as a buffer for bursts, an 8–12% additional committed uplift converts well into ~10–15% usable metered uplift after our allocation.
